Comment: Bulk Silver -> staging -> production. Stage 1 loads the whole window for every account, then Stage 2 promotes one account per Map branch. Substitute ${STAGE_LAMBDA_ARN} and ${PROMOTE_LAMBDA_ARN} before creating the state machine. Execution input: {} for the default window, or {"start_datetime":"...","end_datetime":"..."} / {"delta_minutes":90}, optionally with "account_ids" and "force".

StageSilverDelta.Comment: Claims the run slot, creates the stg_*_bulk tables, loads all 13 tables from Silver and runs the widened stale update. Returns the account_ids the Map fans out over.

Parameters.Comment: The execution input is merged in wholesale rather than field by field: a JsonPath to an absent field (start_datetime on a default-window run) fails the state, and every window field is optional.

VacuumTargets.Comment: One VACUUM ANALYZE pass before the Map. The onboarding pipeline vacuums inside each account's run; at Map concurrency that would mean several concurrent VACUUMs over the same tables.

Catch.Comment: A failed vacuum is not a reason to skip promotion — it only costs query plan quality.

PromoteAccounts.Comment: One branch per account. MaxConcurrency is deliberately low: every branch writes to the same production tables through the same RDS instance.

Catch.Comment: Staging is deliberately left in place on failure so the window can be re-promoted without re-querying Athena. ReleaseRunSlot frees the slot without dropping the tables.

Cleanup.Comment: Drops the stg_*_bulk tables and releases the run slot.

ReleaseRunSlot.Comment: Failure path. Releases the run slot but keeps the staging tables for inspection — a slot left held would otherwise block the next run until STALE_RUN_HOURS elapsed.

PipelineFailed.Comment: Terminal failure — enables Step Functions redrive from the failed state.
PipelineFailed.Cause: See $.error in the execution history for the failing state.
